label: prf:alpha-k-derivation-procedure
title: Proof of alpha k derivation procedure
html:
Proof. The Markov property pins each \mathrm{tr}_M(w_\mu) to z^{n - \mathrm{len}(\mu)} by induction on \mathrm{len}(\mu) (Jones, Theorem 5.1). Cycle-type representatives form a class-function basis on H_n(R, q) at generic q, so the \chi-matrix is invertible — the system has a unique solution. \square

Closed-form available via Wenzl-bridge. By prop:y-lambda-closed-form-wenzl-bridge, y_\lambda(q) has the explicit q-rational expression y_\lambda = s_{\lambda, r}(Q) / \sum_\mu d_\mu s_{\mu, r}(Q) with Q = q^2 and X = Q^r = q^{3/2} / (1 + q - q^2 - q^3 + q^{3/2}), in O(p(n) \cdot \max\text{hooks}) time. The recipe is detailed in prop:y-lambda-recipe-from-partition. The 4-step linear-system algorithm below remains valid as an alternative derivation, and was historically the first method used in this paper.

Algorithm (per-n y_\lambda extraction).

  1. Enumerate partitions of n: \{\lambda^{(1)}, \ldots, \lambda^{(p(n))}\} — gives the unknowns.
  2. Construct cycle-type representatives: for each \mu \vdash n, pick the canonical reduced word w_\mu (concatenation of cycle-rotations on disjoint strand groups; length \sum_i (\mu_i - 1) = n - \mathrm{len}(\mu)).
  3. Compute character matrix: for each (\mu, \lambda), evaluate \chi_\lambda(w_\mu) via Hoefsmit seminormal form (Hoefsmit). Cost dominated by O(p(n)) partitions \times Hoefsmit-matrix size d_\lambda \leq |\lambda|!/\!\prod h_x.
  4. Solve linear system: A \cdot \mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b} with A_{\mu, \lambda} = \chi_\lambda(w_\mu) and b_\mu = z^{n - \mathrm{len}(\mu)}. Output \{y_\lambda\}.

Stratum prefactors \alpha_k at depth k. Once \{y_\lambda\} is known, the depth-k stratum prefactor in the unified mass formula (unified mass formula) is the Markov-pairing of \mathrm{tr}_M with a chosen E_\infty^{0, 0}-page representative r_k of the depth-k class:

  \alpha_k \;=\;
  \langle \mathrm{tr}_M, r_k \rangle
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda_k}
    y_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(r_k),

with \Lambda_k the depth-k stratum (enumeration). The representatives r_k at H_3(R, q) are explicitly identified in (H_3 explicit); analogues for H_n(R, q) at n \geq 4 follow the same pattern (depth-k reduced word of length \geq k).

Witness data.

Jones–Markov weights y_\lambda for n \in \{2, 3, \ldots, 12\} are tabulated in computations/y-lambda-jones-markov-witness.json, generated by the formal derivation. Each table records:

  • partition \lambda \vdash n and curvature-rank \mathrm{depth}(\lambda);
  • Jones–Markov weight y_\lambda (numeric at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps));
  • linear-system condition number and residual.

Output sums consistent with Plancherel-completeness (Plancherel boundedness).

Worked example: H_3(R, q). Three partitions (3), (2, 1), (1, 1, 1); three constraints

  \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \quad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z, \quad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1 \sigma_2) = z^2.

Solution (H_3 explicit): y_{(3)}, y_{(2,1)}, y_{(1,1,1)} are explicit q-rational expressions. The depth-k prefactors are

  \alpha_0 = 1, \qquad
  \alpha_1 = 0, \qquad
  \alpha_2 = z^2, \qquad
  \alpha_3 = h \cdot z^2 + z = z(1 + q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}),

all closed q-algebraic forms (no fitting; verified to 5.5 \times 10^{-17} residual).

Iterative computation pipeline.

The procedure is computationally bounded by the largest Hoefsmit matrix size \max_\lambda d_\lambda. At n = 12 the maximum d_\lambda = 462 (rectangular (4, 4, 4)); the linear system is 77 \times 77. For higher n, sparse seminormal representations and per-partition caching keep the cost feasible. The witness pipeline (the formal derivation) forces sparse Hoefsmit generators, builds the cache once per partition, and reuses across all test words, yielding O(p(n)^2 \cdot \max d_\lambda^3) overall with bounded memory.

CRT-style q-probing and reconstruction. The numeric witness at q_0 represents one ring-map specialisation \iota \colon R \to \mathbb{R}. Each y_\lambda is a q-rational element of R(\!(z)\!) — generically of the form P_\lambda(q^{1/2})/ Q_\lambda(q^{1/2}) with both \deg P_\lambda, \deg Q_\lambda growing in n. The q-parameterised seminormal builder (build_seminormal_matrices(q=...)) evaluates y_\lambda at any canonical evaluation point. Two reconstruction strategies:

Multi-q Padé / rational interpolation. Choose m distinct canonical evaluation values q_1, \ldots, q_m (e.g.
\{1.02, 1.05, 1.08, 1.11, 1.15\} — the formal derivation precedent). Vandermonde-uniquely determines a polynomial of degree \leq m - 1; faithful rational reconstruction y_\lambda = P/Q with \deg P = a, \deg Q = b requires m \geq a + b + 1 probes. An a priori bound from the determinant structure of A(q) gives \deg P_\lambda, \deg Q_\lambda = O(n^2), so faithful rational reconstruction needs on the order of n^2 canonical evaluation points — not 5. Five canonical evaluations suffice for: (i) a degree-4 polynomial fit usable for local sensitivity \partial y_\lambda/\partial q near q_0, (ii) consistency checks against any analytically derived closed form.

Symbolic linear-system solve. For exact rational forms, replace numeric numpy.linalg.solve with sympy over a symbolic q. Cost grows rapidly with p(n), but the output is the exact q-rational y_\lambda. Tractable in pure Python for n \leq 5; larger n needs a compiled character kernel.

Witness data layout. At n \leq 10 the witness records both the canonical q_0 floats and 5 CRT canonical evaluation points \{(q_i, z_i, \mathbf{y}(q_i))\} for verification of any closed form. At n \in \{11, 12\} only q_0 is recorded (canonical evaluation-rebuild cost prohibitive in pure Python; defer to a compiled kernel for higher-n probes).

Closed forms for \alpha_k across n.

n p(n) y_\lambda witness \alpha_k closed form
2 2 available trivial: \alpha_0 = 1, \alpha_1 from singlet
3 3 available done: \alpha_0, \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3 (H_3 explicit)
4 — 12 5 — 77 available \alpha_k pending: requires depth-k representatives r_k at each n

Per-n \alpha_k derivation reduces to: (i) selecting depth-k representatives r_k \in H_n(R, q), then (ii) computing the Markov pairing \langle \mathrm{tr}_M, r_k \rangle via the witnessed y_\lambda. Step (i) is the open work; step (ii) is mechanical once (i) is fixed.

Although the derivation mechanism utilizes the standard Jones-Markov linear system extraction across Wenzl bridges, employing this machinery to extract the mass-spectrum coefficients \alpha_k constitutes a mathematically novel physical framework unique to the Quantum Observable Universe.
